item.title: Michigan State offensive lineman unleashes a fountain of puke during two-point conversion
item.description: Michigan State's Robert Wright Jr. unleashed a vomit-filled two-point conversion block in Pat Fitzgerald's debut win over Toledo Friday night.
item.content:encoded:
This weekend features the first "full" slate of college football, but eagle-eyed fans were able to find some pretty premier programs take the field before Saturday.

Perennial top-25 programs like Missouri, and Utah were in action on Thursday and we were even treated to some college football themed Friday Night Lights.

The vaunted Miami Hurricanes were able to obliterate an undermanned Stanford team out west, and the Michigan State Spartans kicked off the Pat Fitzgerald era in style with a 30-20 win over MAC darlings Toledo on Friday.

SEC LAWYERS, LANE KIFFIN AND DEATH VALLEY: COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S WEEK 1 IS SET FOR FIREWORKS

And it is in East Lansing where we find our story today.

As Sparty was trailing by a single point early in the fourth quarter, quarterback Alessio Milivojevic connected with Rodney Bullard Jr. for a five-yard touchdown to put Michigan State ahead for good.

To put themselves ahead by a whole touchdown and extra point, Fitzgerald and the staff decided to go for two, and that's when offensive coordinator Nick Sheridan reached into his bag of tricks and pulled out the sickest two-point conversion play he had.

Literally.

That's a lot of puke, brother.

This could be karmic payback for making everyone watch Michigan State play in those highlighter green uniforms from a few years ago.

Those were enough to make anyone in attendance need to grab a bucket.

WEEK ONE UPSET SPECIAL: THESE THREE COLLEGE FOOTBALL TEAMS SHOULD BE ON UPSET ALERT THIS WEEKEND

Let this be a note to offensive linemen everywhere who are plying their craft, if you're having trouble picking up twists and stunts along the defensive line, just unleash your pregame meal right as the ball is snapped.

No one is going to want to touch you and your chunder without throwing on a hazmat suit first.

It's brilliant, really.

Oh, and the two-point conversion was good, proving even further that this was a calculated move by the Spartans and right tackle Robert Wright Jr.

It's a fairly untapped technique, considering most linemen I see puking do it in the huddle or right before the ball is snapped.

Wright, on the other hand, waited until after the ball was snapped, picks up a stunting interior lineman, passes off the rush end, and keeps his quarterback clean for a successful two-point try.

That's consummate professionalism right there!

Now all he needs is an NIL deal with Pepto-Bismol and he's in business; make it happen, Sparty!

item.title: Students divided as University of Michigan will hide first-semester grades for 2027 freshmen
item.description: University of Michigan students clash over a pass/fail policy hiding first-semester freshman grades, debating mental health relief vs. study habits.
item.content:encoded:
ANN ARBOR, Mich. — University of Michigan students are split over a new administrative policy that will hide first-semester letter grades for incoming freshmen, with some welcoming the relief from academic pressure while others warn it could coddle students and fail to prepare them for the real world.

Starting in fall 2027, incoming first-year students enrolled in the university’s College of Literature, Science, and the Arts (LSA) will have their first-semester transcript grades designated strictly as pass (P) or no credit (NC). School officials say the pilot program aims to combat a growing "mental health crisis" on college campuses and ease the transition from high school to college. 

"Our goal is to help first-year students acclimate to the demands of college and allow intrinsic motivations to guide personally meaningful academic journeys — core elements of a liberal arts and sciences education," the university stated in its announcement.

COLLEGE STUDENTS EXPRESS STRONG TRUST IN SCHOOL LEADERS DESPITE BROADER PUBLIC CYNICISM: GALLUP

While students will still receive traditional letter grades and feedback directly from professors throughout the term, final marks will not appear on official external transcripts or factor into overall GPAs. The university will retain internal letter grade records for advising, financial aid eligibility, academic awards and scholarships, and other administrative purposes.

Several students told Fox News Digital that easing into college expectations could be a net positive.

"If there are measures to ease the way for high school students coming to [university], I think that's a good thing," said Alexander, an exchange grad student from Austria.

Ella Langlois, an LSA student, said that it does not hurt to give the policy a test run. 

"I do think mental health is always super important," she said.

William Bushey, a civil engineering major, called the decision a "good call."

"I'm an engineer, so I go through all the weeder classes all the time," Bushey said. "There's a lot of successful people who struggle in their first-year classes, but will just pass and then wind up being super successful later on."

Chloe Song, an economics freshman at LSA, agreed that the initial transition can be daunting. 

"I think that's a good call because it's really stressful," Song said.

The LSA is the largest of the university’s 19 schools and colleges, serving approximately 19,700 undergraduate students. University leaders hope the grade-covering policy gives students the freedom to explore challenging electives without fear of damaging their long-term GPAs. Similar pass/fail or hidden-grade policies for first-year students have existed for decades at institutions such as MIT, Caltech, Wellesley, and Swarthmore.

However, not all U-Mich students are on board. Some argue that shielding grading consequences promotes poor study habits and ignores the root causes of student anxiety.

"I think it's kind of silly," said Talan, a freshman neuroscience major. "I know they say it's to curb mental health and stop people from having mental health crises, but I feel like that is our generation having access to media across the world. That's why their mental health is a little worse, not because they’re worried about grades."

"We’re at the University of Michigan — people tried pretty hard to get here," Talan added. "I feel like grades are taken pretty seriously. And if you're going to try, working as hard as someone who gets a C and passes with the same grade as you is kind of demeaning in a way."

Simran, a sophomore business major, suggested that hiding grades avoids teaching resilience.

"I think having more supportive resources is a better solution than hiding grades," Simran said. "I think there's a lot of challenges that you face in college, and challenging coursework is one of them. It's something you just learn to move through. I've definitely done poorly in classes before, but it's an upward battle at times... it's a very important skill to have."

Others expressed concern that the policy will merely delay academic stress until the second semester.

Andrew Spencer, a biology, health, and society major, said that while he might have personally benefited from the break, he believes the policy will ultimately backfire.

"Overall, it's just going to hurt more," Spencer said. "People are just going to slack off and not care about their grades in the first semester, and then not have the skills themselves for the second semester to come in and have a great work ethic."

Monica Diaz, a junior studying psychology and economics, offered a middle ground, noting that while she understands critics' concerns, the single-semester policy isn't permanent coddling.

"I don't entirely agree with that because I think it's just slowly transitioning them into what it's like to be at a school like the University of Michigan," Diaz said. "Obviously, after the first semester they're not going to be coddled anymore, so I don't really think that's entirely true — but I can definitely see the argument."

item.title: Texas opens season against Texas State as Arch Manning faces a make-or-break college football year
item.description: Arch Manning enters a make-or-break season as Texas hosts Texas State in a lopsided Week 1 college football matchup with the under 59.5 play.
item.content:encoded:
We officially have the first full weekend of college football. From now until the end of the year, we get to watch football essentially all day Saturday and Sunday.

Sure, there will be some breaks in there, and some days that won’t have quite as much on the gridiron. Still, I’m pumped to have it back and have more options for sports betting. I mentioned this in another article, but this is not a great week of games, as most are lopsided games.

We will likely have one here between Texas State and Texas, but there is still reason for intrigue.

STEVE SARKISIAN GIVES EMBARRASSING EXPLANATION FOR TEXAS' COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF LOSS: 'WE WERE TIRED'

Money is a major factor in college sports, but with college football being the king of them, there is money galore. I have to imagine that one of the reasons that Texas State agreed to this game is that the school was paid a lot of money to come play Texas.

Texas State went 7-6 last year, so it wasn’t like they were awful. However, the best team they played last year was probably Arizona State. They played Rice in a bowl game, so perhaps that was their toughest game.

Brad Jackson is back under center for Texas State, so you have to imagine the team will at least know the offense well enough to run coherent plays. Last season he was pretty good. He completed 71% of passes, had 21 touchdowns, and seven interceptions, while racking up 3,224 yards. Greg Burrell, who was their secondary running back last year, steps in as the primary back this year. He averaged 6.7 yards per carry last year, but had just 3 touchdowns.

ARCH MANNING ISN’T BACKING DOWN FROM EXPECTATIONS, AND NEITHER IS STEVE SARKISIAN, AS CFP SEMIS AREN'T ENOUGH

In my opinion, this is a make-or-break season for Texas. I’m not saying their coach will be fired, or anything like that. However, I also wouldn’t rule that possibility out.

The bigger thing to me is that they need to figure out what is going on with their quarterback, Arch Manning.

Coming out of high school, he was one of the highest-regarded prospects potentially ever. In his first season as the primary QB, he was fairly average. He completed just 61.4% of passes, but had 26 touchdowns and seven interceptions to go along with 3,163 yards.

It was a tale of two locations for Manning. At home, he was very good, completing 65% of passes and 19 of his 26 touchdown passes. He only had two of his seven interceptions at home as well. They missed the playoffs despite coming into the season as the top-ranked team in football. Manning is projected to be the No. 1 overall pick in the NFL Draft. I just don’t see it happening if he doesn’t take a major step forward.

This is a much easier way to start the year than what Texas had last year, starting on the road against Ohio State (they face them again, but at home next week). This year, Texas should destroy their opponent to start the season. However, Texas only had two wins last year by more than 21 points. They played a tough schedule, but they also played a lot of close games. There is no lack of talent here, but I don’t see this team scoring a ton of points either. I think Manning will play maybe half the game unless he looks awful, and if he looks awful, they won’t have many points. Give me the under 59.5.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed hits back at Israel questions, suggests his name and faith are behind press scrutiny
item.description: Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed suggested reporters press him on the Israel-Hamas war because of his name and faith.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed suggested that reporters press him about the Israel-Hamas war because of his name and his faith. 

Speaking on Detroit Public Radio’s "MichMash" podcast, El-Sayed pushed back on host Zach Gorchow’s line of questioning about the Israel-Hamas conflict, suggesting that his name and Muslim faith play a role in the media attention surrounding the issue.

"You've been asked many times whether you support a two-state solution regarding the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and you generally say you support equal rights to self-determination for Jewish Israelis and Palestinians," Gorchow said. "Can you tell us, what does that mean?"

MICHIGAN DEM HOPEFUL ABDUL EL-SAYED JABS CNN GIVING HIM 'NON-CONSENSUAL COLONOSCOPY' IN RECENT INTERVIEWS

"Zach, with all due respect, this has been hashed and rehashed," El-Sayed began. "This is the MichMash podcast. I'm focused on what's happening for the 10 million people in this state."

El-Sayed then suggested the media’s interest in his stance on the conflict was related to his identity.

MICHIGAN SENATE CANDIDATE CONFRONTED REPEATEDLY OVER ISRAEL’S RIGHT TO EXIST, DEFUNDING THE POLICE

"It's so frustrating to me that people want to make this race about something that's happening 6,000 miles away, when we've got kids who can't afford a next meal here at home," he continued.

The controversial candidate went on to blast the constant line of questioning from members of the press regarding his stance on providing aid to Israel — a topic he has remained staunchly against throughout his campaign.

MICHIGAN SENATE HOPEFUL CALLS AIPAC DONATIONS 'LEGALIZED BRIBERY,' REMAINS SILENT ON OTHER DONATIONS

"I just find it so interesting that I never get asked about this question on the stump," El-Sayed told the host. "But it seems to me that every time I sit down with anybody in the press, it seems that that's the most important question."

El-Sayed continued by suggesting the media’s focus on his stance on Israel could be related to his name and Muslim faith.

EL-SAYED’S HASAN PIKER PROBLEM FOLLOWS HIM TO DEM CONVENTION AS JEWISH VOTERS BREAK RANKS

"It tends to be the first question everybody likes to ask me," he said. "I wonder why? I mean, does it have something to do with my name? Maybe, you know, how I pray?"

He concluded by doubling-down on his assertion that his campaign is focused on the people of Michigan — not the people of Israel.

MICHIGAN DEMOCRATIC SENATE CANDIDATE CLAIMS ISRAEL 'JUST AS EVIL' AS HAMAS

"It's fascinating to me that I'm running to represent ten million people who live here, and you want to ask about people living somewhere else," El-Sayed continued. "And I just think I want to be talking about [the] people living here."

According to data compiled by the Jewish Virtual Library, Michigan is home to 129,225 Jewish residents — which comprise roughly 1.3% of the state’s population.

JEWISH DEMOCRATS ABANDON EL-SAYED FOR GOP RIVAL IN ALL-IMPORTANT BATTLEGROUND STATE

El-Sayed’s comments were of interest to CEO of Axia Public Relations Jason Mudd, who told Fox News Digital his ability to flip the narrative on the press shows a level of message discipline.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"He stayed on message, pivoting to affordability both times he was asked. That's real discipline. But when you listen to the full episode, he never uses the word racist. He questions why the topic keeps coming up and ties it to his name and his faith. He's pointing to bias."

"If El-Sayed were my client, I'd advise him to name the bias claim directly instead of leaving it implied, then answer the follow-up on what his position actually means in the same breath. Right now the framing comes first, and he still hasn't answered the follow-up."

Fox News Digital reached out to El-Sayed's campaign for comment.

item.title: 9 warning signs of identity theft you should never ignore
item.description: Nine identity theft warning signs range from unfamiliar credit inquiries to SIM swap attacks that can quietly drain your bank account funds.
item.content:encoded:
Identity theft can start quietly. You may not see a drained bank account or a maxed-out credit card. The first warning could be a strange letter in the mail, an unfamiliar inquiry on your credit report or a password-reset alert you never requested.

Those little clues are easy to brush off, but catching them early can give you more time to protect your money, credit and accounts. One unusual message does not automatically mean someone has stolen your identity, so do not panic. Instead, verify what happened and pay attention to anything else that looks out of place.

Here are nine identity theft warning signs you should never ignore.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Protect Your Money replay

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Protect Your Money From Today’s Biggest Threats , has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our financial protection checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five simple ways to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. You’ll learn how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed.

Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com

CYBERCRIME LOSSES NEAR $21B: 5 WAYS TO PROTECT YOUR MONEY

A company may contact you after discovering that customer information was exposed. The notice could come from a bank, retailer, employer, healthcare provider, insurer, school or another organization.

Read it carefully. Find out what information may have been involved, when the incident occurred and whether the company is offering steps such as password changes or credit monitoring. Save the notice with your other records.

A breach notice shows possible exposure, not confirmed identity theft. Still, it is a good reason to review your accounts and strengthen your security.

Check your credit reports for hard inquiries you do not recognize. A hard inquiry generally appears when a lender reviews your credit after you apply for credit.

Also look for new accounts, unfamiliar addresses, collections accounts or loans you never requested. Identity thieves may use stolen information to apply for credit before you notice anything unusual.

Check all three major credit bureaus rather than relying on a single report. Details can differ from one report to another, so reviewing only one may leave gaps.

If you find an inquiry or account that does not belong to you, contact the lender using a trusted phone number or website, rather than contact information from a suspicious message.

A bill for a credit card, utility service, medical account or buy-now-pay-later purchase you did not make is a serious warning sign. So is a call from a debt collector about a debt that does not belong to you.

Do not ignore the notice simply because you believe it is a mistake. Ask the organization for details, dispute the account and keep copies of your correspondence.

Be cautious about sharing personal information with an unexpected caller. If you need to contact a company, find its official number independently.

Review checking, savings, credit card, payment app, investment and retirement accounts regularly. Look for small test charges, unfamiliar withdrawals, new payees, password changes, profile updates or transfers you did not authorize.

Scammers sometimes begin with a small transaction to see whether an account is active. Other times, they try to take over the account entirely.

Contact the financial institution immediately through its official app, website or statement. Ask what steps are needed to secure the account, replace cards, investigate transactions and protect any linked accounts.

Turn on account alerts for purchases, transfers, password changes and other important activity. Alerts are useful, but they work best when you still review statements yourself.

Pay attention to unexpected letters or online notices from the IRS, Social Security Administration or a state agency. Examples include a tax return you did not file, benefits you did not request or a claim connected to an employer you do not recognize.

Do not respond using a link or phone number in an unsolicited message. Visit the agency's official website or use a phone number from a statement or a previously verified account.

Keep every notice. Government-related identity theft can take time to resolve, and a clear record of dates and communications may help.

A phone that unexpectedly loses service can have an innocent explanation, such as an outage or billing problem. But it can also be a sign that someone transferred your number to another device or took over your mobile account.

That is exactly what happened to Patricia Escriva, whose phone suddenly lost service before scammers used a SIM swap attack to get into her accounts and steal thousands of dollars. We broke down her story and what you can learn from it in The CyberGuy Report podcast: How hackers drain your bank account in minutes.

If your phone suddenly goes offline and you cannot explain why, treat it as a warning sign. Contact your wireless provider right away from another phone and ask whether there was a recent SIM change, number transfer or account update. A SIM is the small card or digital profile that connects your phone to a mobile network.

Once your number is secure, review important accounts for password resets or login attempts. Ask your carrier about an account PIN or other protections against unauthorized changes.

HEALTHCARE DATA BREACH EXPOSES 3.75M PATIENT RECORDS

An unexpected password-reset email, multifactor authentication code or sign-in alert may mean that someone is trying to access an account. It may also be a fake message designed to trick you into clicking a link.

Do not share a verification code with anyone who calls or messages you. Open the account through its official app or type the website address yourself, then review recent activity and change the password if needed.

Start with your primary email account. Email often acts as the doorway to password resets for banking, shopping, healthcare and other services. Use a long, unique password and turn on multifactor authentication, which requires an extra verification step beyond your password.

Avoid reusing passwords. If one website is breached, a reused password may give criminals an opportunity to try the same combination elsewhere.

A sudden wave of calls, texts or emails that use your correct name, address, family details or account information deserves attention. This does not prove identity theft, but it may indicate that personal data is circulating among scammers.

Be especially cautious when a message creates urgency, demands payment, asks for a verification code or tells you to move money to "protect" it. Banks, government agencies and legitimate companies do not need you to hand over a one-time code to keep your account safe.

Instead of replying, contact the organization through a trusted channel. Then review your accounts, credit reports and recent security alerts.

An unfamiliar mailing address on a credit report, a changed email address on an account or a notification that your identity was verified somewhere you do not recognize can signal an attempted takeover.

Review account recovery information, authorized users, linked devices and connected apps. Remove anything you do not recognize and change the password from a trusted device.

If the change involves a bank, credit card, phone provider or government account, contact that organization promptly. A small profile change can be an early step in a larger attempt to control the account.

First, slow down and verify the information. A suspicious text may be a scam, and a legitimate account alert may be the result of a family member's purchase or a forgotten subscription.

If the activity is confirmed or you cannot explain it, take these important steps:

Use a trusted number or official app. Ask the organization to secure the account and investigate.

A credit freeze restricts access to your credit file, making it harder for someone to open new credit in your name. Place a freeze with all three major credit bureaus if appropriate for your situation.

A fraud alert asks lenders to take extra steps to verify your identity. It provides another layer of protection and works differently from a credit freeze.

Change important passwords, use a password manager to create and store strong, unique passwords, review recovery settings and add account protections through your wireless provider.

Check banking, credit cards, payment apps, investments, retirement, healthcare, utilities and government services.

Save breach notices, screenshots, dates, names, dispute numbers and copies of letters.

If you confirm that someone has used your identity, report it to the Federal Trade Commission at IdentityTheft.gov. The site will help you create an FTC Identity Theft Report and build a personalized recovery plan. You can also use that report when working with credit bureaus, businesses and debt collectors to dispute fraudulent accounts or information. Some companies may also ask for a police report.

If your information appears in a breach, you may not be able to remove it completely. Focus on making the exposed information less useful: freeze your credit, secure your accounts, limit unnecessary public information and keep watching for new warning signs.

You can take many important steps to protect yourself, including checking your accounts, using unique passwords and freezing your credit. An identity theft monitoring service can add another layer by watching for signs that your personal or financial information may be misused.

Depending on the service and plan you choose, monitoring can include credit reports, checking and savings accounts, investments and 401(k) accounts, bank account takeovers, home title changes, phone takeovers, identity verification, dark web exposure, data breaches and social media activity.

That broader monitoring can be helpful because identity theft can show up in more places than your credit report. If fraud occurs, restoration support may also help reduce the burden of dealing with calls, paperwork and disputes.

Monitoring works best as an added layer of protection rather than a replacement for good security habits. Continue reviewing your accounts, watching for unusual activity and acting quickly when something looks wrong . See my tips and best picks on Best Identity Theft Protection at Cyberguy.com

NEW BANK SCAM LAWS COULD STOP SUSPICIOUS PAYMENTS

Identity theft often gives you warning signs before serious damage is done. A strange charge, an account you do not recognize or even a password-reset alert you never requested can be your cue to take a closer look. Trust your gut when something feels off, verify what happened and act quickly to lock down your accounts and credit. A few minutes spent checking now could save you a much bigger headache later. The key is to stay alert without living in fear. Keep an eye on your accounts, use strong security protections and know what steps to take if your information ends up in the wrong hands.

item.title: Deprogrammed: Ex-OnlyFans manager finds Jesus and goes on a mission to save young women
item.description: Former OnlyFans manager Victoria Sinis says sexual liberation is "actually the thing that's crushing us" and shares how Christian faith set her free.
item.content:encoded:
Once trapped under the temptation of wealth from the digital exploitation of young women’s bodies, Victoria Sinis is now free from a sordid life as an OnlyFans manager after reclaiming her faith in Jesus.

"Coming from someone that believed the lie that sexual liberation and sexual empowerment was to sleep with people, to show off your body as much as possible, to make money off doing that, and now coming into Christian faith… I see things with a totally new set of values," Sinis told Fox News Digital.

"We paint [sexual liberation] as freedom, but it’s actually the thing that’s crushing us… [It is] actually the thing that's destroying you. It's the thing that's crushing you. It's a thing that makes you more insecure. It’s the thing that makes you feel worse," she continued.

PLAYBOY'S CELEBRITY-DRIVEN RELAUNCH FACES CREDIBILITY TEST IN ONLYFANS ERA, EXPERT SAYS

Sinis, whose work as a manager for an OnlyFans agency in Australia began during the pandemic in an effort to improve her finances while reducing the amount of hours she was working in hospitality, now highlights her experience online, exposing the dark underbelly of the adult industry while saving girls from falling prey to the platform.

"Once you open up the door for sexuality to be able to have any desire that you want fulfilled, people have to understand it's a never-ending pit. It just keeps going. And so the reason why faith has such strong values around sexuality is because it understands the dangers of when you open that door — it's very hard to close it," Sinis said.

"When you understand in a faith lens of, ‘Wow, there's a reason for this, and it's made in a specific and particular way to be able to best express this thing,’ it's the most freedom you can ever have," she said.

"I saw firsthand how things like OnlyFans are really destroying men…. There is an entire multi-billion dollar industry that is targeting men, to be able to harness their weakest essence to get them addicted to these platforms, to make money off of them. And in return, it is heightening their loneliness, their depressions, their anxiety, their disconnectedness, their struggles with being able to build healthy relationships," she continued.

'HARRY POTTER' ACTOR SAYS ONLYFANS VIDEOS EARNED HER MORE THAN HER ENTIRE ACTING CAREER

"These platforms are really destructive for men, and we need to understand that the more we encourage this, the more that we're actually hurting men as much as we are hurting women," she relayed.

Sinus was catapulted over time into searching for a good deed to redeem herself and outdo the bad she felt she was doing. That journey led her back to the church she visited as a child, where she encountered a sermon that "instantaneously clicked" with her spirit, reconnected her with Jesus and helped her leave the industry for good.

Sinis, who now travels the world speaking about her experience in the adult industry, points to social media as a main culprit in glamorizing lifestyles that make children and young people idolize career choices like OnlyFans.

"Parents are so unaware of what is truly influencing their child. If they have a phone, if they have a laptop, if their friend has a phone, if their friend has an iPad, and they have unlimited Internet access to any type of social media platform, they're going to be influenced by those things unless values are instilled within them that help them to understand that what they're seeing online is not real," she revealed.

FORMER DISNEY STAR DAVID HENRIE REJECTED 'SECULAR' HOLLYWOOD LIFESTYLE AFTER LIFE-CHANGING MONASTERY VISIT

"I had two 15-year-olds at a private Catholic school in a fantastic area in Melbourne, Australia, tell me that they loved watching this OnlyFans influencer, because she seemed happy and can travel. And so sometimes it's the most innocent of things, but they're now equating to OnlyFans with being happy and travel[ing] — so now they believe that the only way to be happy and to travel is through OnlyFans," Sinis added.

"This is the sex industry. It is the same consequences, the same mental health ramifications and the same struggles as any other woman in the sex history. And we need to treat it that way and understand that the struggles that the girls have in OnlyFans really is the same as anyone in escorting prostitution, brothels.. and that way we're able to act in accordance with that and be able to truly help these women to leave [the industry]," Sinis said.

An OnlyFans spokesperson told Fox News Digital, "OnlyFans was designed to empower creators to control and monetize their content, and individual creators determine what content they choose to create and how they engage with their audience. Since the platform was established in 2016, more than $30 billion has been paid out to creators around the world, including more than $6 billion in 2025."

item.title: Trump pardons Jay-Z associate Emory Jones after federal drug conviction
item.description: Alice Marie Johnson revealed Trump granted clemency to 30 individuals, including Emory Jones, a Roc Nation executive and Jay-Z's longtime associate.
item.content:encoded:
Emory Jones, longtime friend and business associate of Jay-Z, has been granted a pardon by President Donald Trump.

Jones, who is now an executive in Jay-Z's Roc Nation, was sentenced to nearly 16 years in 2000 on federal drug charges. Thanks in part to a letter from the hip-hop mogul, his sentence was reduced by 37 months, but now, Trump has given him a completely clean slate.

The news was shared this week by Alice Marie Johnson, who was pardoned by Trump in 2020 after being sentenced to life in prison on a nonviolent drug charge in 1996. She now works with the White House as the "pardon czar."

JELLY ROLL GRANTED PARDON BY TENNESSEE GOVERNOR IN CHRISTMAS SEASON CLEMENCY DECISION

"Yesterday was a powerful day for second chances," Johnson wrote on Instagram. "I am deeply grateful to President @realdonaldtrump for granting clemency and pardons to 30 deserving individuals whose cases we carefully reviewed and brought forward—and to the White House Counsel team, led by Will Scharf, for the hard work behind these decisions."

She added, "Among them is Emory Jones, who served nearly 16 years in federal prison and came home determined to build a different life. Today he is an entrepreneur and creative leader whose journey reminds us how much people can grow—and how much good they can still do."

TODD CHRISLEY RECALLS EMOTIONAL PHONE CALL WITH DAUGHTER SAVANNAH AFTER CONTROVERSIAL TRUMP PARDON

In 1999, Jones pleaded guilty to a charge of conspiracy to distribute cocaine. The following year, he was sentenced to 188 months, nearly 16 years, in prison, with five years supervised release.

Jones' legal team submitted a request for a reduction of his sentence in 2009, and as part of their request, they submitted a series of letters from people familiar with Jones, including Jay-Z.

In a letter to the judge, Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter, wrote that he'd be offering Jones an executive assistant job with Roc Apparel Group upon his release, with a starting salary of $50,000.

"As you might expect, this position needs to be filled as soon as possible," he wrote. "It is my strong desire to have Mr. Jones fill this position. I have known Mr. Jones for 15 years. I believe his attributes, including intelligence, interpersonal skills and solid work ethic will be a significant asset for my organization."

In another letter, Jones himself wrote about his conviction, saying, "Of all the excuses that I could have attributed my demise to, I chose not to use a single one. Excuses are tools of the incompetent and only build monuments to nothingness."

He also included mention of his support system, including Jay-Z, writing, "When a person or people make sacrifices and devote themselves to supporting you through the adversity of incarceration, you owe them. Nothing monetary because you can't put a price on love and support. However, you do owe them the privilege and opportunity to see you do something extremely positive with your life."

Jones was resentenced to 151 months, still with five years supervised release, shaving 37 months off of his original sentence.

Today, he's the head of Lifestyle at Roc Nation, and he also has an executive role in fashion brand Paper Planes, which he and Jay-Z founded in 2014.

item.title: Lady Frost eyes Major League Wrestling women's title, touts 'incredible roster'

item.content:encoded:
Lady Frost has her eyes on the Major League Wrestling (MLW) Women’s World Championship and is willing to do whatever it takes get some gold wrapped around her waist.

Shotzi found herself a challenger in Lady Frost over the last few weeks after she rose in MLW to grab the title from Shoko Nakajima on MLW "Fusion" back in June. Frost came out to confront Shotzi on last week’s episode, appearing to declare herself the top contender for the belt.

COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON OUTKICK

"Well, if you've seen anything that I've done lately – because you did say you've been watching — I am a fighter. I have everything to prove and that's the No. 1 spot and I deserve it. That's it. It's as simple as that," Lady Frost told OutKick Dropkick in a recent interview.

Frost said she would give "everything" to get that championship.

"Literally everything. That's the goal," she said. "And I'm willing to do whatever it takes to get it."

Frost was one of MLW’s marquee signings this year to bolster its women’s division. She shared some light on why she decided to sign with MLW back in April.

"So, the conversation that we had was very valuable to me because they've been watching me for a very long time, not just my work in the past few years," she said. "And I think it's important for someone to believe in you creatively and as a performer in general. And I think they have all the confidence in the world in me. And that's exactly what I wanted to hear.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

"I felt like it was a good fit because all of the women there are trying to prove something because they're either brand new, trying to make a name for themselves, trying to rebuild, or just make this women's division even tougher than it already is."

MLW also has alliances with Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre (CMLL) and Stardom, which allows for the roster to mix it up with opponents from around the world.

Frost said those relationships were a part of the intrigue.

"I think I've done numerous tours in CMLL and that's a great fit for me. And then the girls of Stardom, obviously those are great matches," she said. "I love working those girls. And then there's the independents, which I feel like was very healthy for me to get back into creatively.

"It's not all about hitting your times and being on camera and doing things appropriately. It's reminding ourselves why we do this and what we're fighting for, and most times it's the fans, right? So, having a little bit of everything right now while focusing on that title for MLW has really been great for my career."

Frost is set to take on Corinne Joy at MLW’s Kings of Colosseum event.

The top stars on the roster will be on display, including Killer Kross, Josh Bishop, Diego Hill, Templario and others. The event will be free on YouTube, beIN Sports and Veeps.

"We have an incredible roster. We have great production. I think it's unique in its own way and it's not something that some people might feel overproduced in a way that feels artificial," Frost added. "I think it feels very raw and real. And you see so many different unique styles. And yes, we partner with CMLL, so you will see that lucha style. You're going to see that grittiness. You're going to see darkness. There's something for everyone."

item.title: Legendary agent explains how Deshaun Watson's $230 million contract has crippled the Browns
item.description: Deshaun Watson's $230 million fully guaranteed contract has crippled the Cleveland Browns' salary cap, with an $86.2 million dead cap hit looming in 2027.
item.content:encoded:
The Cleveland Browns hoped when they acquired Deshaun Watson in 2022 that he would have a major impact on the franchise, and revisiting the trade four years later, they weren’t wrong.

What kind of impact, exactly, has Watson had on the Browns? A disastrous one. The team gave up five draft picks, including three first-rounders, and then signed Watson to a five-year, $230 million fully guaranteed contract, the largest amount of guaranteed money given to a player in NFL history.

Watson was suspended for 11 games in 2022 after facing several sexual assault allegations from his time with the Houston Texans. Watson has played only 19 games in four seasons with the Browns and has disappointed on the field. Legendary sports agent Leigh Steinberg explained that while Watson has hurt the Browns on the field with his play, his exorbitant contract has crippled the team's salary-cap flexibility.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"The fact that they've got that contract on Cleveland's roster, which is all guaranteed, makes it very difficult to do what is advanced caponomics, which is to take a high salary, all of which counts against the cap, and supplement it with a new signing bonus and extend the contract out over a series of years," Steinberg told OutKick in a recent interview.

"That's the modus operandi to fit talented players into a cap. But when all the money is guaranteed, there's no way to escape the cap hit."

The Watson contract is so onerous that the Browns were forced to push his cap hit into the future beyond the term of his five-year contract by using void years. Early in Watson’s contract, they lessened his cap hit in order to build around him and pushed a ton of money into the future.

Now they are feeling the constraints of Watson’s deal.

Here are Watson’s cap hits from 2022 through 2030: In 2022, it was $9.4 million, followed by $19 million, nearly $28 million, nearly $36 million and a $40.2 million cap hit this season.

LEGENDARY SPORTS AGENT TALKS ABOUT THE RAMS USE OF 'CAPONOMICS' TO BRING AARON DONALD OUT OF RETIREMENT

Next season, despite not being on the Browns' roster after his contract expires this season, Watson will have an astronomical $86.2 million cap hit, followed by a $25.7 million cap hit in 2028, nearly $17 million in 2029 and $8.9 million in 2030. In all likelihood, the Browns will have to further leverage their future cap space because carrying an $86.2 million cap charge for a player who will likely not be on their roster next year would be crippling to a front office trying to build a competitive roster.

If the Browns decide to leave that $86.2 million entirely on next season’s cap, it would account for more than a quarter of their salary cap. Despite the cap continuing to rise year after year, a cap hit that high is not tenable for a team trying to win games and spend big in free agency.

The Browns, despite having a 9-10 record in Watson’s starts, named him their Week 1 starting quarterback. Watson has completed 61.2% of his passes for 3,365 yards with 19 touchdowns and 12 interceptions in his tumultuous tenure.

Watson has not played since he tore his right Achilles tendon in October 2024, and re-tore it during rehab in January 2025.

The Browns hope Watson can recapture some of the magic he had with the Houston Texans this season under new head coach Todd Monken because, if he can, his massive cap hit won't hurt as much.

But Steinberg isn’t sure Watson will play well enough to fend off backup Shedeur Sanders, and start the whole season.

"Now, if Deshaun Watson were to come back to what he was at Clemson or with Houston, he started out like he was going to have a spectacular career and then because of offseason issues and injuries, the wheels came off. And so, while he's been designated the starter now, it's unclear whether or not he'll hold that till the end of the year," Steinberg said.

Watson is only 30 years old, and Steinberg mentioned quarterbacks who have been effective despite being much older than Watson.

"He's not too old. As we've seen with Aaron Rodgers and Tom Brady, players can play deep into their 40s and still be effective at that position, but he's got to be a little rusty," Steinberg said.

While the Browns hope Watson can be effective this season, it would come four excruciating seasons later than they would have hoped after giving him the most guaranteed money any player had received in NFL history.

Across football and baseball, Steinberg’s clients include Steve Bartkowski, Steve Young, Troy Aikman, Warren Moon, Bruce Smith, Thurman Thomas, Kordell Stewart, Jeff George, Ben Roethlisberger, Myron Rolle, Matt Leinart, Mark Brunell, Ricky Williams, Howie Long, Eric Karros and Dusty Baker, among others.
